Nestled within the historic heart of Hanoi, Hang Duong Street stretches from the bustling Đồng Xuân Market down towards the serene Hoàn Kiếm Lake, embodying a charming blend of ancient tradition and modern vibrancy. Centuries ago, this narrow thoroughfare served as a vital hub for merchants transporting honey sugar, rock sugar, and hoa mai sugar from the fertile Red River Delta to the imperial capital.

The architectural landscape of Hang Duong Street is characterized by its narrow width and the presence of tube houses, which bear the distinct imprints of ancient Vietnamese architecture. These structures, with their glossy brown exteriors and moss-stained balconies, stand as testament to the enduring charm of old Hanoi.
